ideas.name: SK Hynix Inc.
ideas.thesis: SKHY appeared in all 6 overnight screens — the highest conviction signal in today's digest. A fresh Reuters-reported Intel partnership catalyst (Sep 16), BofA PT raise to $268 (from $250, Sep 13), HBM4 mass shipments underway, a 40 trillion KRW buyback program, and a tightening global DRAM shortage combine to create a multi-leg setup. The stock has pulled back ~11% from its $199 high on sentiment-driven AI-regulation headlines, not fundamentals, offering a re-entry vs. a ~49–50% analyst target gap.
ideas.catalyst: Reuters partnership talks with Intel reported Sep 16, 2026; Q3 earnings proxy via Micron (Sep 30); SK Hynix own earnings expected October 2026
ideas.edge: BofA 12-month PT $268 vs. ~$179 current = ~50% implied upside gap; net income +108% YoY; ROIC >70%; 40T KRW buyback active; DRAM shortage structurally tightening supply pricing
ideas.bull_case: Intel partnership confirms US-footprint strategy, triggering a re-rating; DRAM shortage accelerates pricing power; buyback provides a floor and Oct earnings deliver upward revisions.
ideas.bear_case: US-Korea geopolitical friction or AI-export regulation headlines could reprice the multiple quickly; macro rate environment (10Y at 5%+) compresses high-beta Korean ADRs; Intel deal talks could fall through.

ideas.name: NVIDIA Corporation

A hard earnings date of November 17, 2026 creates a defined pre-earnings run window. The stock sits ~40–52% below average analyst target with revenue estimates revised up 10.3% in the past 3 months. Options (call spreads, Oct/Nov expiry) are the preferred structure given macro rate volatility.

ideas.bear_case: 10Y at 5%+ compresses high-multiple growth stocks; any hiccup in Blackwell/Vera Rubin supply chain or new export restrictions could derail the November earnings bar; rising-rate environment makes holding outright stock risky.

ideas.name: Invesco QQQ Trust
ideas.thesis: QQQ appeared in 4 of 6 runs as a tactical macro vehicle. However, with 10Y at 5.01%, VIX firming, and 1–2 more hikes possible, screens were split between a near-dated call spread to capture the relief bounce through Oct 28 FOMC and a put spread as a portfolio hedge — suggesting defined-risk structures on both sides.

ideas.name: Micron Technology, Inc.
ideas.thesis: MU appeared in 2 of 6 screens with high conviction votes (2/2) around a hard-dated binary: Q4 FY2026 earnings after market close September 30, 2026. Street consensus projects +350% revenue YoY and +900% EPS YoY on the back of the HBM/DRAM AI memory supercycle; the prior quarter beat consensus by 17.6%. This is the first major semiconductor earnings post-Fed hike and serves as a direct read-through for SKHY and the broader memory complex. Defined-risk options (call spread expiring Oct 3) are preferred given the binary nature of the event.
ideas.catalyst: Q4 FY2026 earnings confirmed after market close September 30, 2026
ideas.edge: Wall Street consensus: revenue +350% YoY, EPS +900% YoY; prior Q3 beat consensus by 17.6%; global chip sales +135% YoY in July; structural HBM4/DRAM shortage tightening into the print
ideas.bull_case: DRAM shortage and HBM4 ramp drive another blowout beat; management raises Q1 FY2027 guidance above consensus; stock re-rates toward analyst targets in a compressed-valuation catch-up move.
ideas.bear_case: Elevated expectations (900% EPS growth) create a 'buy the rumor, sell the news' risk; post-Fed macro volatility could overwhelm even a beat; outright stock holding ~$926 creates large dollar-loss exposure if guidance disappoints.

ideas.name: Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund
ideas.thesis: XLE appeared in 2 of 6 screens as a macro hedge and sector-driven play. APPEC September 2026 consensus has formally shifted to treating the Strait of Hormuz disruption as a structural supply baseline through the end of the current administration — not a spike event. With Brent at $104–109/bbl, Goldman flagging $120+ spike risk, and Reuters analyst consensus projecting Brent averaging $134, energy earnings (Exxon profits doubled, Chevron +~400% YoY net income) are still unfolding. XLE +30% YTD has not fully priced a sustained $100+ regime.
ideas.catalyst: APPEC Sep 2026 structural consensus on Iran-Hormuz; Fed hike reinforcing oil-as-inflation-hedge bid; energy sector Q3 earnings season beginning October 2026
ideas.edge: Goldman flagging $120+ Brent spike risk; Reuters analyst consensus projects Brent averaging $134; XLE historically lags crude in spike but catches up in sustained high-price regimes — current regime structurally fits the latter; underlying energy EPS still being revised higher
ideas.bull_case: Structural Hormuz closure keeps oil above $100 through year-end; energy earnings season delivers further upside surprises; rate-driven inflation fears add an inflation-hedge bid to the sector.
ideas.bear_case: A diplomatic resolution to the Iran conflict — however unlikely per APPEC consensus — would reprice crude sharply lower; recession fears from sustained 5%+ rates could crush industrial demand and oil prices; XLE already +30% YTD limits near-term upside relative to risk.
